css-cubic-bezier.description: Design CSS easing curves with control points, compare presets, simulate elapsed time, and copy or download transition and animation CSS.

meta.title: CSS Cubic Bézier Editor
meta.description: Design CSS easing curves with control points, compare presets, simulate elapsed time, and copy or download transition and animation CSS.
meta.keywords: cubic bezier, CSS easing, transition, animation, timing function, overshoot

cubicBezier.graphHint: Horizontal: elapsed time. Vertical: output progress. P1 and P2 are control points; the dashed diagonal is linear easing. Move the slider to follow the curve.
cubicBezier.hint: X coordinates must be between 0 and 1. This editor accepts Y coordinates from −5 to 5. Use plain decimals with up to 4 decimal places.
cubicBezier.rules: The curve starts at (0, 0) and ends at (1, 1). Y values outside 0–1 allow anticipation or overshoot. Progress is evaluated by solving the time coordinate, not by treating the curve parameter as time. Paste either declaration inside a CSS rule; choose which property to animate and its duration separately.
cubicBezier.emptyResult: Enter control points or choose a preset, then generate CSS.
cubicBezier.invalidX: Enter an X coordinate from 0 to 1 with up to 4 decimal places.
cubicBezier.invalidY: Enter a Y coordinate from −5 to 5 with up to 4 decimal places.
